URL.documentsDirectory is the sandboxed Documents folder. The translation derived it from java.io.tmpdir, whose parent is the app data directory next to shared_prefs, databases and files, so createAndGetDirectory() and the settings import wrote there. Documents.directory is <filesDir>/Documents and moves what older versions left in the old place once, before its first use.

UIDocumentPickerViewController(asCopy: true) hands over a file URL of a copy in the temporary Inbox, named after the picked file. DocumentPicker.copy copies the document to <cacheDir>/Inbox/<display name> off the main thread (a stinger from a cloud provider could block it for seconds) and passes its path on the main thread; onUrl then moves it to Documents/ReplayTransitions/<stinger id>.<extension> with ReplayTransitionsStorage.add, as the Swift StingerView does. The generated block copied on the main thread with the provider's last path segment as the name, into filesDir, and passed a file: URI that File(url) cannot open. HSYS.7 to HSYS.9 and HSYS.16 to HSYS.21 remove the rest of that block.

Nothing sets Keychain.appContext, so every load returned nil and every store was dropped: tokens were lost on each restart.

With HSYS.13: SecItemCopyMatching reports a status and never throws. A failing Android Keystore must make the keychain empty, not throw out of Settings.load(), which would replace the settings with the defaults.

hooks.note: See HSYS.12.

When the Keystore key is lost (restore to a new device, Keystore reset) the old file can never be decrypted and EncryptedSharedPreferences.create throws on every start, so no token could be saved again. Like iOS after a restore, KeychainPreferences drops what a working key cannot decrypt, keeps everything still readable, and throws only when the Keystore itself fails.
